title: A Parish for the Portrait
premise: Vesper Eastwick, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has catalogued a thousand deaths, receives two letters the same morning: one confessing to a drowning thirty years ago in the coastal parish of Saltmere, the other promising that 'the tide will give up what it took' on a named date. Sent to assess a suspicious claim on the drowned man's estate, Vesper finds a village built on an alibi — six witnesses who all remember the same night identically, too identically. As he unpicks their rehearsed memories, he discovers the confessing letter was written by someone protecting the real killer, and that his own late mother's name appears in the parish register. At the spring tide, the sea surrenders a locked strongbox; inside is proof that the victim staged his own death and the 'murder' was a cover for those who helped him vanish. The ending: Vesper chooses to bury the truth, granting the found family of Saltmere its inheritance of peace while claiming his own belonging among them.
about_author: Zephyrine Ishikawa is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck claims along the English coast before turning to fiction. They write mysteries where memory is both evidence and mercy, and live within earshot of a tidal estuary.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Vesper Eastwick opens his morning post to find twin letters in identical handwriting: a confession to a thirty-year-old drowning, and a promise that the tide will return what it took. His photographic memory flags a detail no one should know. POV: Vesper. Beat: unease — the past has found his address.

chapters.title: The Claim at Saltmere
chapters.summary: Assigned to investigate a life-insurance claim reopened by an anonymous tip, Vesper travels to the decaying seaside parish of Saltmere, where the drowned man's cottage still stands untouched. He notices the village feels curated, like a stage set. POV: Vesper. Beat: arrival and quiet wrongness.

chapters.title: Six Who Remember
chapters.summary: Vesper interviews the six surviving witnesses to the night Thomas Wrenn went into the sea. Their accounts match word for word — including a mistake in the weather report. Someone taught them a story. POV: Vesper. Beat: the first crack in the alibi.

chapters.title: The Widow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wrenn's widow, Maren, now the parish's matriarch, feeds Vesper supper and deflects every question with warmth. He memorizes her kitchen and realizes she's been expecting him for years. POV: Vesper. Beat: charm as armor; he likes her anyway.

chapters.title: A Name in the Register
chapters.summary: Searching the parish records for claim history, Vesper finds his mother's maiden name entered the year before her death — she lived here once. The case stops being professional. POV: Vesper. Beat: personal vertigo; grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Niece
chapters.summary: Tracing the letters' handwriting, Vesper meets Ivy Calloway, niece of the confessed writer, a dying old fisherman who refuses to retract or explain. Ivy, sharp and guarded, becomes his reluctant ally. POV: alternating Vesper/Ivy. Beat: alliance formed out of mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Ivy shows Vesper the tideline caves where Wrenn's boat was found, empty and dry below the waterline — impossible unless it never sank there. The confession begins to look like a shield. POV: Vesper. Beat: the mystery inverts.

chapters.title: Rehearsed Rain
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts two witnesses separately with the false weather detail; one breaks down, insisting she only repeated what Maren told them all to say. But why would Maren lie about a drowning? POV: witness then Vesper. Beat: guilt without crime.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Date
chapters.summary: The threatening letter names a date: the highest spring tide of the year, three weeks out. Someone wants Vesper present when the sea gives something back. He decides to stay. POV: Vesper. Beat: commitment; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Mother's Room Above the Chandlery
chapters.summary: Following the register, Vesper rents the room his mother once kept above the old chandlery and finds her initials carved beneath the sill, beside another set: T.W. She knew Thomas Wrenn. POV: Vesper. Beat: intimacy with the dead; loneliness answered.

chapters.title: Ivy's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ivy reveals her uncle's confession letter arrived with a solicitor's note: keep it sealed until someone came asking about Wrenn. She was waiting for Vesper without knowing it. POV: Ivy. Beat: her stake deepens; trust tentatively offered.

chapters.title: The Man Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Insurance archives yield a second claim: a body matching Wrenn washed ashore in Cornwall two years after his death, misidentified and buried. Either Wrenn died twice or never died at all. POV: Vesper. Beat: revelation — the victim may be the architect.

chapters.title: Maren Unbound
chapters.summary: Vesper lays the Cornwall evidence before Maren. She finally speaks: Wrenn was fleeing debts and dangerous men, and the village hid him by killing him on paper. The alibi was a gift. POV: Maren then Vesper. Beat: sympathy complicates suspicion.

chapters.title: The Men from the City
chapters.summary: Two strangers arrive asking the same questions Vesper did — collectors hunting Wrenn's hidden assets, willing to hurt people to find them. The stakes turn physical. POV: Vesper. Beat: external threat; the village closes ranks around him.

chapters.title: Broken Window, Broken Story
chapters.summary: The chandlery is ransacked; the strangers take the parish register. Vesper reconstructs its contents from memory, page by page, becoming the archive himself. POV: Vesper. Beat: his gift becomes the village's lifeline.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Third Letter
chapters.summary: Ivy's uncle, near death, dictates a fragment: the strongbox Wrenn left behind holds not money but proof that could ruin the collectors' employers — and it surfaces only on the great tide. POV: Ivy. Beat: motive clarified; countdown tightens.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Vesper and Ivy stake out the tideline caves ahead of the tide and catch the collectors searching early. A tense standoff ends when the whole village appears silently on the shingle behind them. POV: Vesper. Beat: found family made visible; fear met with solidarity.

chapters.title: The Spring Tide
chapters.summary: At the appointed hour, the sea withdraws further than anyone remembers and exposes the cave mouth where Wrenn cached his strongbox. Vesper reaches it minutes before the collectors do. POV: Vesper. Beat: climax begins; the promise fulfilled.

chapters.title: What It Took
chapters.summary: Inside the box: ledgers proving the collectors' employers ran a fraud ring, plus a letter from Wrenn — alive until recently — entrusting the truth to whoever remembered enough to find it. Vesper's memory was the intended key all along. POV: Vesper. Beat: climax; identity and purpose converge.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Archive
chapters.summary: With the collectors exposed and arrested through the ledger evidence, Vesper faces the last decision: publish everything, including how the village faked a death, or let the confession stand as the official record. He remembers his mother's carving. POV: Vesper. Beat: moral crux.

chapters.title: Buried in Plain Water
chapters.summary: Vesper files his report confirming the original drowning verdict, sealing the village's secret forever, and mails the fraud evidence anonymously to authorities. Maren reads his face and knows what he gave up. POV: Maren then Vesper. Beat: sacrifice completed; grace exchanged.

chapters.title: A Parish for the Portrait
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Vesper stays on, taking the room above the chandlery permanently. The parish commissions a portrait of its six witnesses — and asks him to sit among them as the seventh. For the first time, he belongs to a picture instead of filing one. POV: Vesper. Beat: resolution; belonging earned and accepted.
